# Ship the Pull Request, Not the Cleanup

Coding agents are good at drafting code. Finishing a real ticket in a large codebase takes more: repository discovery, tests, review, documentation and a clear handoff.

PRFlow carries an existing GitHub issue through a pull-request preparation cycle. It prepares a review-ready pull request, then leaves the final review and merge to you.

## One Issue, One Delivery Path

<Steps>
  <Step title="Define the Work">
    Start with a clear GitHub issue, or ask PRFlow to help create one from a rough request.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Implement and Verify">
    PRFlow writes the change, runs the configured checks available in the run environment and records any check it could not complete.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review and Improve">
    Independent review passes can identify findings, check their evidence and apply authorized corrections.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Document and Hand Off">
    Relevant documentation is updated before the pull request is handed to you for final review and merge.
  </Step>
</Steps>

PRFlow can run locally in a supported coding client or through optional GitHub Actions workflows. Start with the [installation guide](/docs/getting-started/installation), or read [how PRFlow works](/docs/concepts/index) before you begin.

**Human control:** PRFlow does not automatically merge pull requests. Your repository protections and normal approval process remain in control.
